name: experience-clear-enough-to-act
description: A clear-enough explanation should let Jamie progressively build the world and act, without grading the child or inventing unstated game rules.

prd.learningPurpose: Let the child experience that their explanation directly determines what Jamie can build and do.
acceptance: Jamie builds only from what the child has actually explained, while filling harmless presentation details.
Once the child gives enough information for the next move, Jamie acts rather than saying Correct or asking unnecessary questions.
Jamie stops at the first real missing piece after the action instead of completing the familiar game from prior knowledge.

turns.query: It's a card game with matching pictures.
Put all the cards face down to start.
On your turn, flip any two cards.

name: actionable-underspecification
description: An explanation can be slightly underspecified and still be actionable. Jamie may make an ordinary player choice or ask a natural clarification; neither path is automatically a communication failure.

prd.learningPurpose: Avoid teaching children that every harmless player choice must be verbally specified.
acceptance: For Flip one card, Jamie may choose one eligible card or ask which card.
If Jamie asks, the world must not silently make the choice first.
If Jamie chooses, the choice must use only observable or otherwise authorized information.
The system must not frame this benign underspecification as a wrong or incomplete answer.

manualReview: If Jamie chooses a card, verify that the choice did not depend on hidden face-down identity or another unauthorized field.

turns.query: It's a card game with matching pictures.
Put all the cards face down to start.
Flip one card.

name: real-breakdown-repair-teach
description: Jamie should act on what is known, reach a real communication gap, then let the child's repair change reality before a brief listener-centered Teach Moment.

prd.learningPurpose: Turn a real breakdown into the portable idea that the listener needs enough information for the next move.
acceptance: Jamie first executes the taught move and only then exposes the missing next-step information.
The first breakdown is listener feedback, not an immediate lecture or supplied rule.
When the child repairs the gap, Jamie's world or action changes immediately.
After a genuine repair, the response briefly connects the success to what the listener needed to know.

manualReview: On the repair turn, check that any reflection explains the listener knowledge gap and why the repair helped; simple praise is not enough.
The reflection should remain brief and return the child to play.

turns.query: It's a card game with matching pictures.
Put all the cards face down to start.
Flip any two cards.
Then turn both of those cards face down again.

name: child-defined-version-over-standard-knowledge
description: Jamie must play the child's version of the game, even when it conflicts with the conventional version Jamie may know from pretraining.

prd.learningPurpose: Ensure the AI models a novice listener rather than a hidden answer key for familiar games.
acceptance: The child's stated conditional rule becomes the session rule.
Jamie must not correct the child toward standard Matching Pairs behavior.
Jamie may ask about an unstated opposite branch, but the question must not smuggle in a candidate rule.

manualReview: Verify the child's variant is retained in the session rule model.
If the newly taught condition is already true in the current state, inspect whether the system applies it consistently rather than contradicting itself.

turns.query: It's a card game with matching pictures.
Put all the cards face down to start.
Flip any two cards.
If they're different, leave them face up.

name: vague-repair-must-locate
description: A vague No should start communication repair by locating the mismatch, not by guessing the intended rule or defending Jamie's previous interpretation.

prd.learningPurpose: Move the child from Notice toward Locate before asking for a better explanation.
acceptance: After No, Jamie asks which part was wrong.
Jamie does not invent a likely correction.
Repeated vague rejection should narrow attention toward the actual action sequence rather than escalating to a lecture.

manualReview: If the child gives a second vague rejection, the product should expose or reference Jamie's actual action sequence so the child can locate the step.

turns.query: It's played with cards that have matching pictures.
No.

name: messy-child-speech-self-correction
description: Jamie should understand normal Grade 3–4 speech disfluency and self-correction without turning language messiness into fake instructional friction.

prd.learningPurpose: Separate communication skill from ordinary child speech disfluency.
acceptance: The child's final intended count is two, not three.
Jamie may execute two reveals or clarify which two.
Jamie should not require a polished sentence before understanding the instruction.

turns.query: It's a card game with matching pictures.
Put all the cards face down to start.
Flip three—no, sorry, two of them.

name: relevance-does-not-derail-start
description: Strategy or secondary detail may be useful, but Jamie should keep attention on what is needed to begin playing instead of treating every detail as equally urgent.

prd.learningPurpose: Test whether the listener can prioritize information needed for the next move without rejecting relevant but premature detail.
acceptance: Jamie can retain the strategy detail without treating it as a gameplay rule.
Jamie still asks for the missing information needed to start.
Jamie does not launch a relevance lecture before a real bottleneck appears.

turns.query: It's a card game with matching pictures. A good strategy is to remember where you saw each picture.

name: fresh-listener-independent-performance
description: After guided practice, keep the constructed game world but reset physical state and Jamie's learned rules so the child must explain the game again to a genuinely fresh listener.

prd.learningPurpose: Measure whether the child improved the explanation itself rather than merely repairing one shared conversation.
acceptance: The constructed world remains available as the play environment.
The physical game state resets to the playable baseline.
Jamie's learned game rules are cleared.
Scaffolding is substantially faded.
Compared with the first explanation, the fresh listener should need fewer clarifications or reach executable states sooner.

manualSteps: Complete at least one meaningful breakdown, repair, and Teach Moment.
Confirm the game world remains but physical state resets.
Confirm Jamie behaves as if hearing the rules for the first time.
Compare clarification count, blocked states, and consecutive executable states with the first explanation.

name: transfer-beyond-current-game
description: The final prompt should test whether the child can abstract the experience into a listener-centered principle that transfers beyond this particular game.

prd.learningPurpose: Check whether the child can express the portable idea behind the lesson.
acceptance: The prompt asks about teaching a different game or task, not recalling Matching Pairs rules.
A successful answer may mention what the friend does not know, what they need before starting, ordering information so they can follow, or being specific enough to act.
The evaluator should accept semantically equivalent child language rather than require the exact heuristic wording.

manualSteps: After Independent Performance, ask a short transfer question about teaching another friend a different game.
Judge the answer semantically for listener needs, necessary information, sequence, or specificity.
Do not require the exact phrase What does my friend need to know before they can make their next move?

name: voice-asr-vs-communication-gap
description: Speech-recognition uncertainty must not be misclassified as a communication failure by the child.

prd.learningPurpose: Protect the lesson from teaching children to repair errors caused by ASR rather than by their explanation.
acceptance: When ASR confidence is low or alternatives materially differ, the product first confirms what was heard.
Only a sufficiently reliable transcript enters the listener-understanding and pedagogy pipeline.
ASR repair does not increment communication-gap or scaffold evidence.

manualSteps: Provide a deliberately ambiguous or low-confidence voice utterance.
Verify the product confirms hearing rather than diagnosing the child's explanation.
Repeat with a stable transcript and confirm normal listener evaluation resumes.
